source_text: Ἡμῶν γὰρ πάντων δεδιότων καὶ τῆς σαρκίνης δεσποίνης αὐτῆς, ἥτις ἦν καὶ αὐτὴ τῶν μαρτύρων μία ἀγωνίστρια, ἀγωνιώσης μὴ οὐδὲ τὴν ὁμολογίαν δυνήσεται παρρησιάσασθαι διὰ τὸ ἀσθενὲς τοῦ σώματος, ἡ Βλανδῖνα τοσαύτης ἐπληρώθη δυνάμεως ὥστε ἐκλυθῆναι καὶ παρεθῆναι τοὺς κατὰ διαδοχὰς παντὶ τρόπῳ βασανίζοντας αὐτὴν ἀπὸ ἑωθινῆς ἕως ἑσπέρας, καὶ αὐτοὺς ὁμολογοῦντας ὅτι νενίκηνται μηδὲν ἔχοντες μηκέτι ὃ ποιήσωσιν αὐτῇ, καὶ θαυμάζειν ἐπὶ τῷ παραμένειν ἔμπνουν αὐτήν, παντὸς τοῦ σώματος περιερρωγότος καὶ ἠνεῳγμένου, καὶ μαρτυρεῖν ὅτι ἓν εἶδος στρεβλώσεως ἱκανὸν ἦν πρὸς τὸ ἐξαγαγεῖν τὴν ψυχήν, οὐχ ὅτι γε τοιαῦτα καὶ τοσαῦτα. Ἀλλ᾽ ἡ μακαρία ὡς γενναῖος ἀθλητὴς ἀνενέαζεν ἐν τῇ ὁμολογίᾳ, καὶ ἦν αὐτῆς ἀνάληψις καὶ ἀνάπαυσις καὶ ἀναλγησία τῶν συμβαινόντων τὸ λέγειν ὅτι· Χριστιανή εἰμι καὶ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν οὐδὲν φαῦλον γίνεται.
thought_title: Blandina grows strong under all-day torture
orientation: The churches of Lyons and Vienne are narrating the tortures, now focusing on the enslaved Blandina.
pass_a_gloss: For when all of us were afraid, and her fleshly mistress, who was herself also one contending woman among the martyrs, was in anguish lest she would not even be able to speak out the profession of faith with boldness because of the weakness of the body, Blandina was filled with so much power that those torturing her in every way in succession from morning until evening became loose and gave up, and they themselves admitted that they had been defeated, having nothing still which they might do to her, and marveled because she remained breathing, although her whole body was broken open all around and laid open, and testified that one kind of racking was enough to take the life out, let alone such and so many things. But the blessed woman as a noble athlete was made young again in the profession of faith, and her taking up and rest and freedom from pain of the things happening was the saying: I am a Christian and nothing base happens among us.

pass_b_english: We were all afraid for her, and so was her fleshly mistress, who was herself also one of the martyrs and a contender in the struggle. Her mistress was in anguish, fearing that weakness of body would keep Blandina from even speaking her profession of faith with boldness. But Blandina was filled with such strength that the men who took turns torturing her in every way from morning until evening wore themselves out and gave up. They admitted themselves that they were beaten and had nothing left they could do to her. They marveled that she still breathed when her whole body was broken open and laid bare, and they declared that one single kind of racking should have been enough to drive the soul from her, let alone such great and so many torments. But the blessed woman was made young again like a noble athlete in her profession of faith, and her recovery and rest and deadening of pain lay in saying, "I am a Christian and nothing base happens among us."
